content.summary: Guidance on use of transthoracic echocardiography (TTE), computed tomography (CT) including coronary CT angiography (CCTA), and cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) for patients presenting with suspected acute coronary syndromes (ACS) or alternative diagnoses.

TTE.recommendation: All patients presenting with cardiogenic shock (CS) or haemodynamic instability should undergo emergency transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) to identify underlying cause(s), assess left and right ventricular (LV/RV) function and look for mechanical complications.
TTE.notes: TTE can be useful to suggest alternative aetiologies associated with chest pain (e.g., acute aortic disease, RV signs in pulmonary embolism).

Computed_tomography_overview.recommendation: CT is often the diagnostic tool of choice to rule out alternative potentially life‑threatening differential diagnoses of ACS such as pulmonary embolism or aortic dissection (use ECG-gated contrast CT angiogram with full coverage of thoracic aorta and proximal head and neck vessels).
Computed_tomography_overview.limitations: Generally CT does not have a role in patients with suspected ongoing acute coronary occlusion where emergency invasive coronary angiography (ICA) is the priority.

Coronary_CT_angiography_CCTA.evidence: Multiple trials including BEACON, ROMICAT II and RAPID‑CTCA investigated CCTA in ED patients with suspected NSTE‑ACS; trials in the era of high‑sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs‑cTn) assays are most relevant now.
Coronary_CT_angiography_CCTA.findings: No reduction in in‑hospital duration of stay or hospital admission in CCTA arm vs patients investigated with hs‑cTn in some studies; a default approach using early non‑invasive CCTA in suspected NSTE‑ACS did not improve 1‑year clinical outcomes and was associated with modest increase in duration and cost of hospital stay.
Coronary_CT_angiography_CCTA.recommendation: Default use of CCTA as first‑line imaging in suspected NSTE‑ACS is not recommended, but CCTA may add value in selected clinical settings (e.g., observe zone with inconclusive cTn and ECG). A normal CCTA has high negative predictive value to exclude ACS and is associated with excellent outcomes.
Coronary_CT_angiography_CCTA.limitations: Utility of CCTA may be limited in patients with tachycardia, established coronary artery disease, prior stents, or extensive coronary calcification.

Post_discharge_CCTA.recommendation: Systematic use of CCTA in rule‑out patients after hospital discharge may identify obstructive or non‑obstructive plaque and guide preventive medical therapies; can help risk stratify selected low‑risk NSTEMI patients who may not require invasive angiography if normal.

Cardiac_magnetic_resonance_CMR.role: CMR delineates cardiac structure and function, provides assessment of myocardial perfusion and injury pattern; imaging test of choice when poor echocardiographic windows preclude diagnostic evaluation.
Cardiac_magnetic_resonance_CMR.use: Can be used with or without stress testing to evaluate myocardial ischemia or alternative causes of chest pain/injury.
